edges.description: Accumulated SH3BP2 amplifies immunoreceptor signal transduction.
Hyperactive signaling drives inflammatory cytokine output.
TNF-alpha and hyperactive signaling promote osteoclast differentiation.
An expanded osteoclast pool resorbs jaw bone.
Resorbed bone is replaced by giant-cell-rich fibrous tissue.

nodes.description: Denosumab is an anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody that blocks osteoclast formation and activity; because cherubism lesions are giant-cell/osteoclast rich, high-dose denosumab has been used off-label with positive outcomes, though pediatric use requires monitoring for rebound hypercalcemia.

evidence.reference_title: Successful treatment of adult cherubism with a 60 mg denosumab 6-monthly regimen.
evidence.snippet: high-dose denosumab has  also been trialed in children with cherubism with positive outcomes

nodes.description: TNF-alpha together with RANKL signaling and the intrinsic hyperactivity of SH3BP2-mutant precursors greatly increases differentiation of monocyte or macrophage lineage cells into bone-resorbing osteoclasts, which are characteristically enlarged.

evidence.reference_title: SH3BP2 cherubism mutation potentiates TNF-α-induced osteoclastogenesis via NFATc1 and TNF-α-mediated inflammatory bone loss.
evidence.snippet: SH3BP2 cherubism mutation potentiates TNF-α-induced osteoclastogenesis via NFATc1

nodes.description: The expanded, hyperactive osteoclast population aggressively resorbs the trabecular bone of the mandible and maxilla, creating the expanding radiolucent lesions characteristic of cherubism.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding c-Abl-binding protein SH3BP2 cause cherubism.
evidence.snippet: excessive bone degradation of the upper and lower jaws

nodes.description: Resorbed jaw bone is replaced by a proliferative fibrovascular stroma containing numerous multinucleated giant cells (osteoclast-like), the histologic hallmark of the cherubic lesion. Expansion of this tissue enlarges the jaws and deforms the face.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding c-Abl-binding protein SH3BP2 cause cherubism.
evidence.snippet: followed by development of fibrous tissue masses, which causes a characteristic facial swelling
proliferative fibroosseous lesions limited to the mandible and maxilla

nodes.description: As an adaptor, accumulated SH3BP2 potentiates signaling downstream of myeloid immunoreceptors, increasing SYK and ERK-MAPK pathway activation in macrophages and osteoclast precursors and lowering their threshold for activation by M-CSF and RANKL.

evidence.reference_title: Increased myeloid cell responses to M-CSF and RANKL cause bone loss and inflammation in SH3BP2 "cherubism" mice.
evidence.snippet: Mutant myeloid cells show increased responses to M-CSF and  RANKL stimulation, and, through mechanisms of increased ERK 1/2 and SYK  phosphorylation/activation

nodes.description: Hyperresponsive SH3BP2-mutant macrophages overproduce tumor necrosis factor alpha. In the knock-in mouse model the cherubism-like phenotype is rescued by TNF-alpha deficiency, identifying macrophage TNF-alpha as the central inflammatory driver; TNF-alpha is also expressed in human cherubism lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Increased myeloid cell responses to M-CSF and RANKL cause bone loss and inflammation in SH3BP2 "cherubism" mice.
evidence.snippet: they form macrophages that express high levels of  TNF-alpha and osteoclasts that are unusually large.

evidence.reference_title: SH3BP2 cherubism mutation potentiates TNF-α-induced osteoclastogenesis via NFATc1 and TNF-α-mediated inflammatory bone loss.
evidence.snippet: TNF-α is expressed in human cherubism lesions

nodes.description: Recurrent missense mutations cluster in exon 9 of SH3BP2, within the peptide that binds the ubiquitin-ligase adaptor Tankyrase. The mutations abolish Tankyrase-directed poly-ADP-ribosylation and RNF146-mediated ubiquitination of SH3BP2, so the adaptor protein escapes proteasomal degradation and accumulates to abnormally high levels in myeloid cells.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding c-Abl-binding protein SH3BP2 cause cherubism.
evidence.snippet: seven mutations in the SH3-binding protein SH3BP2 (MIM 602104) on chromosome 4p16.3 that cause cherubism
Approximately 80% of affected individuals have the disorder as the result of a heterozygous gain-of-function pathogenic variant in SH3BP2.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of Tankyrase-mediated destruction of 3BP2 is the underlying pathogenic mechanism of cherubism.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that Tankyrase, a member of the  poly(ADP-ribose)polymerase (PARP) family, regulates 3BP2 stability through  ADP-ribosylation and subsequent ubiquitylation by the E3-ubiquitin ligase RNF146  in osteoclasts.

nodes.description: Tacrolimus, a calcineurin inhibitor, blocks the calcineurin-NFATc1 axis required for osteoclast differentiation and has produced clinical and radiologic improvement in aggressive pediatric cherubism.

evidence.reference_title: The calcineurin inhibitor tacrolimus as a new therapy in severe cherubism.
evidence.snippet: After tacrolimus  therapy, the patient showed significant clinical improvement, including  stabilization of jaw size and intraosseous osteogenesis.
